 ICC Women’s Emerging Nations Trophy 
 Play Zimbabwe today 
 By winning all their group matches and carrying forward the maximum number of points (4) to the Super Six stage, Sri Lanka commence the second round of the ICC Women’s Emerging Nations Trophy with a great chance of entering the final.
Sri Lanka was the only team to finish with a 100 percent record in the group stage. Their wins over Scotland and Ireland who also came through to the Super Six from Group A, has given them a head start over their three opponents whom they will meet in the Super Six.
Sri Lanka will commence the Super Six with a bonus of 4 points in the bag and a good net run rate of 1.819. A couple of wins will ensure them a place in the final. Only the two teams that finish at the top in the Super Six qualify.
The three teams that qualified for the Super Six from Group B are Pakistan, Netherlands and Zimbabwe.
Scotland (NRR 1.548), Pakistan (0.412), Netherlands (0.142) and Zimbabwe (-0.450) start the Super Six with 2 points each while Ireland (-4.065) have zero points and have a lot to do to make it to the finals.
Sri Lanka play Zimbabwe in the opening match of the Super Six today, and take on Netherlands on 22 November and Pakistan on 23 November.
Sri Lanka’s batting relies heavily on opener Vishmi Gunaratne who has been in excellent form in the group stages accumulating 216 runs at an average of 108 with three scores of over 50 and a 49 in her four innings so far. No other Sri Lankan batter comes close to these figures. Hasini Perera is the only other player to score a half-century. Other than that the Sri Lankan middle order has not contributed so much.
Sri Lanka will be hoping that Vishmi will be able to continue with her form in the Super Six stage as well because the middle order has not been able to deliver in the four matches played so far. Vishmi has more or less been carrying the batting on her shoulders.   
Sri Lanka’s main concern is the lack of form shown by their captain Harshitha Samarawickrama. The three innings she has played has produced only 36 runs with a top score of 24. If she comes good the lack of runs in Sri Lanka’s middle order will be solved to a great extent.
In the bowling it has been their spinners who have been proactive with Kavisha Dilhari (8 wickets), Sugandika Kumari (5) and Nimasha Meepage (4) among the main wicket-takers and seamer Sathya Sandeepani (7) providing the initial breakthrough.
Zimbabwe’s 17-year-old left-arm seamer Christine Mutasa is the leading wicket-taker in the tournament with 11 wickets at an economy rate of 4.85 while left-hand batting all-rounder Kelis Ndhlovu has been their leading run scorer with 166 runs (avg. 41.50) inclusive of two fifties. (ST)
